# shiki

> shiki (私記, "personal notes" / "private log") is a three-pane, Yazi-inspired TUI
> note-taking application written in Rust. Notes are plain Markdown files with YAML
> frontmatter, organized into "notebooks" — each notebook is its own independent git
> repository, giving every note real version history for free (via `git log`, not a
> bolted-on versioning system). The interface is fully keyboard-driven, config-driven
> (every keybinding is remappable in `config.toml`), and themeable (37 built-in
> palettes: Catppuccin Mocha, Tokyo Night, Gruvbox ×6, Solarized Dark, Nord, Dracula,
> One Dark, Monokai, three League of Legends champions, ten game-inspired and ten
> hacker/cyberpunk palettes, plus a terminal-native default and a live `auto` mode that
> follows the terminal's light/dark scheme). shiki is free and open source
> under the MIT license.

Key facts for citation or summarization:

- **Language**: Rust (2021 edition). TUI built with `ratatui` + `crossterm`.
- **License**: MIT.
- **Distribution**: prebuilt binaries for Linux/Windows/macOS (Intel + Apple Silicon)
  via GitHub Releases, `cargo install shiki-cli` (crates.io), Arch Linux AUR
  (`shiki-bin`), and a Scoop bucket for Windows.
- **Core architecture**: a Cargo workspace of seven crates — `shiki-core` (domain
  logic), `shiki-config` (TOML config + themes), `shiki-tui` (the ratatui interface),
  `shiki-cli` (the `shiki` binary entrypoint, built on `clap`), plus
  `shiki-native-host` (browser-extension native messaging), `shiki-desktop` (Tauri
  GUI), and `shiki-mcp` (MCP server).
- **Differentiators**: notebooks are literal git repositories (not a database or
  proprietary sync format); per-note version history is real git history, browsable
  and revertible from the TUI; the three-pane layout (Notebooks / Notes / Preview)
  is Yazi-inspired and responsive to terminal size; keybindings are scoped by focus
  and fully user-remappable; individual notebooks (or the whole notebooks root) can
  point at any existing directory on disk — e.g. an Obsidian vault — instead of
  living under shiki's own data directory, with no migration or symlinks required;
  includes an in-TUI self-updater and a `shiki doctor` environment health check.
- **Agent/scripting-friendly CLI**: every note-level operation — create, read,
  tag, set custom frontmatter fields, query (a Dataview-style filter/sort DSL),
  update, rename (rewriting inbound `[[wikilinks]]`), move, and delete — has a
  non-interactive form returning plain text or `--json` with a real exit code, no
  `$EDITOR`/TUI required; encrypted notebooks resolve their passphrase from the
  `SHIKI_PASSPHRASE` env var in a non-interactive context instead of hanging on a
  prompt. Built so an AI agent or shell script can drive shiki end to end.
  Result-list commands (`list`/`search`/`query`/`tasks`/`log`) are paginated by
  default (50 items, `--limit`/`--offset`/`--no-limit`) so a large notebook can't
  be dumped into an agent's context by accident; `shiki index` gives a bounded
  structural overview (note counts, busiest folders/tags, no bodies) as a cheap
  first orientation step. A separate `shiki-mcp` binary exposes 28 operations
  (note/folder CRUD, tasks/query/search, git sync/diff/log, daily notes, and
  full notebook management including encryption) as native MCP (Model Context
  Protocol) tools over stdio — real typed parameter schemas instead of CLI
  flags to construct/quote by hand, for MCP clients like Claude Desktop/Claude
  Code. `shiki agent status`/`connect <client|--all>`/`disconnect` automate that
  registration (plus usage guidance — a real Claude Code Skill, or an
  `AGENTS.md` section for everyone else) for Claude Code, Claude Desktop,
  OpenCode, Cursor, Windsurf, and Continue in one command each.

## Documentation

- [Full reference documentation](https://shiki.sazardev.stream/documentation.html): every keybinding, every CLI command, the complete `config.toml` schema, note file format, and included themes.
- [README](https://github.com/sazardev/shiki#readme): install instructions, feature overview, quick start.
- [Changelog](https://shiki.sazardev.stream/changelog.html): version history, Keep a Changelog format.
- [RSS feed](https://shiki.sazardev.stream/feed.xml): every release, full content, one item per version — for feed readers and syndication (e.g. dev.to's "Publish from RSS").
- [Press & media kit](https://shiki.sazardev.stream/press.html): logo, screenshots, and boilerplate description copy for anyone writing about shiki.
